task.description: WF-02 Step 3b -- hard gate on test coverage for REQ-072's 7 acceptance criteria. ORDERING NOTE: Step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER authoring) was merged into Step 2a -- ELIXIR-DEV wrote test/letflow/api/context_test.exs and test/support/req072_probe.ex in the same commit (c434e2c) that implemented lib/letflow/api/context.ex, per the fully-detailed test-case spec already in the validated design doc (Section 2.3/3.3/4). No separate TEST-DESIGNER dispatch occurred this run. Flagged per dispatch instructions; gate procedure unaffected.

result.summary:
Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-072 entry verbatim (7 acceptance criteria), the design doc in full, and test/letflow/api/context_test.exs + test/support/req072_probe.ex + lib/letflow/api/context.ex + lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex directly (not from any prior agent's summary).

AC-to-test mapping (all 7 covered, all real/runnable, no placeholders):
  AC1 (trace id on assigns; no Process.put/get or ETS; moduledoc states the translation) -- grep -rn "Process\.(put|get)|:ets\." lib/letflow/api/ re-run myself: zero hits (exit 1, no match). Moduledoc section 'No process dictionary, no ETS, anywhere in this module' (context.ex:33-46) present and states the Logger.metadata/1 distinction. No mechanical grep-assertion exists inside the ExUnit suite itself (design section 2.4 only calls for a bare shell grep run by each gate, not an ExUnit test asserting on it) -- checked design section 2.4 explicitly: it prescribes 'a bare grep, run by ELIXIR-DEV ... and re-run independently by SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/REVIEWER, each per their own gate' -- it does not ask for an ExUnit-level assertion, so this is not a coverage gap, it is the design's own specified verification shape, and I re-ran it as my own gate's copy of that chain.
  AC2 (log correlation) -- context_test.exs:71-96, 'log correlation (AC2)' describe block. Read it end to end: uses capture_log([metadata: [:trace_id]], fn -> ... end) rather than the design's plain capture_log/1, with an inline comment explaining why (default :logger format prints no metadata keys). Verified this is legitimate test-authoring judgment, not a cover: the test still asserts the trace id string appears in the captured log text (log =~ trace_id) AND that the response header carries the same value -- exactly AC2's 'demonstrated by a test capturing both.' The explicit metadata: [:trace_id] option is required to make Logger.metadata/1's effect observable at all under this project's logger config; omitting it would make the test pass vacuously only if capture_log ever printed metadata by default, which it does not, so the adaptation does not weaken what is proven.
  AC3 (scoped_repo_opts/1 derives prefix solely from auth_context; ignores path/query/header hints) -- context_test.exs:99-157, 4 tests: conflicting-hints test (path param, query param, x-tenant-id header all set to tenant B while auth_context says tenant A; asserts tenant A's schema wins), 1-arity signature test (function_exported?/3 checks against arity 1/2/3/4), and two error-path tests (:missing_auth_context, :invalid_tenant_id). No skip, no TODO.
  AC4/AC5 (cross-tenant 404 byte-identical to never-existed 404; equal query counts) -- context_test.exs:160-243, 'cross-tenant 404 is byte-identical...' describe block. Read end to end. See below for the soundness check (point 7 of my dispatch).
  AC6 (no function takes a caller-supplied tenant/schema/prefix arg) -- covered by the AC3 1-arity test (mechanical/compiled-code check) plus moduledoc section 'No function here takes a tenant/schema/prefix argument' enumerating all 3 public functions by name.
  AC7 (moduledoc explains why no cross-tenant existence check is added, citing INV-5) -- moduledoc section 'Why no cross-tenant existence check is added anywhere (AC7, INV-5)' (context.ex:66-90) states the three-part argument (caller-supplied-arg violation, query-count asymmetry, information leak) and cites INV-5 by name. This is a documentation-content AC, not independently machine-testable beyond CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's Step 1b prose check and REVIEWER's Step 2d re-read -- both already performed; I independently re-read the section myself rather than trusting either prior sign-off, and confirm the prose is present and substantively correct.

Re-ran the tests myself: mix test test/letflow/api/context_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs test/letflow/router_test.exs -- Result: 32 passed, 0 failures. Confirms ELIXIR-DEV's handoff claim exactly; REQ-071's own two test files (api_pipeline_integration_test.exs, router_test.exs) still pass unchanged with assign_trace_id/1 mounted ahead of AuthPipeline.

No skipped coverage: grepped context_test.exs for @tag :skip, 'TODO', and commented-out assertions -- none found. All describe blocks contain real, unconditional assertions.

Fixture isolation: each test/describe block in the 'scoped_repo_opts/1' and 'cross-tenant 404' groups calls TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 with a unique slug_prefix per describe block (req072-a/req072-b for AC3, req072-cross-a/req072-cross-b for AC4/AC5), which internally generates a random UUID-suffixed slug per call (Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1) and registers on_exit teardown before provisioning -- confirmed via test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:172-201. No shared hardcoded tenant/schema id anywhere in context_test.exs. The req072_probe.ex fixture table is created only inside each freshly-provisioned tenant schema per test run via replay_migrations/2 with a narrow migration_source, and the whole file is async: false specifically because Ecto.Migrator needs an unshared connection -- documented in the test file's own moduledoc, matching the established precedent (tenant_provisioning_test.exs, auth_pipeline_test.exs). No hardcoded secrets or connection strings found in either test file.

Self-sufficiency: every test in the AC3/AC4/AC5 describe blocks provisions its own tenant fixtures in its own setup block; no test reads state left behind by a sibling test. Confirmed by re-running the full context_test.exs file in isolation (see mutant-probe run below) -- ran cleanly to completion independent of file/test order.

Point 7 -- cross-tenant-404 test soundness, independently measured, not asserted: applied a real mutant to lib/letflow/api/context.ex's scoped_repo_opts/1 in the working tree, replacing its schema derivation with a query that ignores the caller's own conn.assigns[:auth_context][:tenant_id] and instead resolves whichever tenant was most recently provisioned (simulating an actual leak class -- a scoping bug that silently substitutes a different tenant's schema). Ran mix test test/letflow/api/context_test.exs against the mutant: Result: 9/11 passed, 2 failed -- one of the two failures was exactly the AC4/AC5 'byte-identical 404' test, which raised RuntimeError: test setup error: expected no row for id="..." (the not_found_response/4 helper's own guard against the fixture ever finding a row, which is precisely a leak-detector: under the mutant, scoped_repo_opts(conn_a) returned tenant B's schema, so Repo.get found tenant B's real row where it should have found nothing). This is direct, measured proof the test is not vacuously true -- it would fail loudly against a genuinely leaking implementation, not just against a differently-shaped one. The other failure was the pre-existing AC3 negative-input test (:invalid_tenant_id case), also correctly triggered by the same mutant for an unrelated reason (both tests share the same leak path). Reverted the mutant via git checkout -- lib/letflow/api/context.ex immediately after this measurement; confirmed via git status --porcelain lib/ test/ (empty output) and a full re-run of all three test files, which returned to Result: 32 passed, 0 failures -- quoted both per the mandatory revert-and-verify requirement for any temporary probe.

All 7 acceptance criteria have real coverage, no skipped/placeholder tests, fixtures are isolated and self-sufficient, and the AC4/AC5 test was independently proven to discriminate a genuine leaking implementation from a correct one via a measured mutant run, not by assertion. PASS.
